newsitem.title: USA: How anguished caller alerted police to Versace murder.
newsitem.headline: How anguished caller alerted police to Versace murder.

text.p: "Please, immediately, please," Gianni Versace's chef implored a 911 operator moments after the fashion designer was shot down on the steps of his mansion.
The chef, Charles Podesta, telephoned from inside the house at 8:44 a.m. on July 15 as the fashion designer lay bleeding to death outside.

Miami Beach police on Monday released copies of the 911 tape in which an anguished, breathless Podesta pleads for police to come quickly. Later in the three-minute, 10 second tape, he says. "Why aren't they here yet. My God, we're only a block away."
At one point a woman can be heard screaming in the background.
As the dispatcher took the call at the Miami Beach police headquarters, Podesta gives the address and repeats "Yes, a man's been shot."

Caller: "I don't know. He was walking in front of his home. It's Gianni Versace. He was entering his house. We just heard gunshots. We ran outside. He's on the steps of his house ... please immediately please."
She tells Podesta to stay on the line to give them information and asks if Versace is breathing.
Dispatcher: "I need you to go and check for me."
Later, she says: "What did you say the gentleman's name was, sir?"
Dispatcher: "OK and did you say you heard the gun shot?"
Caller: "We all heard it. We, we didn't know what it was. It was three or four loud pops. We didn't know what it was.
Toward the end of the tape, Podesta says: "He's not moving, he's not moving. Who would have done something like that?"
Versace, who was opening the gates of his mansion on Ocean Drive after walking back from a local cafe, died from two gunshot wounds to the head.

Police named Andrew Cunanan, a gay prostitute wanted for four other murders in other states, as the only suspect and launched a massive manhunt for him. Cunanan was found eight days later on a houseboat two miles (3 km) away. He had committed suicide.
